producer_report.summary: Added a read-only D111 host-rules check in athena-core (host_rules.rs). It does plain `gh api` GETs of the rules/branches view for athena/records and main. It reports force-push forbidden, deletion forbidden and up-to-date required as in force, not in force, or unknown. The module is registered in lib.rs. CHANGELOG and the design doc are updated, and gh.rs has a doc note. The previous send-back was a reporting gap only, so this round I made no code changes and re-ran the checks.

checks_run.note: No error returned; the output file was outside my reach, so I did not read the full output.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: tests feed fixture replies in the rules/branches shape (JSON list of rule objects) and assert: athena/records with a non_fast_forward rule => force-push forbidden in force; a deletion rule => deletion forbidden in force; main with a required_status_checks rule whose parameters.strict_required_status_checks_policy is true => up-to-date required in force.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core host_rules` ran 8 tests, all passed, including rules_in_the_reply_are_reported_in_force.

criteria_check.criterion: Tests assert an empty list `[]` reports all rules as not in force, and that a required_status_checks rule with strict_required_status_checks_policy false (or absent) reports up-to-date as not in force; a partial list (only non_fast_forward) reports force-push in force and deletion not in force.

A recording fake Runner test asserts the check issues only GET calls to `repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/athena/records` and `.../rules/branches/main` (not the classic /protection endpoint), with no method override and no field/body arguments, so no host setting changes.
criteria_check.evidence: Test only_plain_gets_of_the_rules_view_are_issued passed. It asserts the exact args ["api", path] for both calls.

criteria_check.criterion: A test where the runner returns an error (e.g. 403 or 5xx) or unparseable JSON asserts the affected rules are reported as unknown/error, not as 'not in force' and not as in force.
The report names each of the three rules and its state in plain text, e.g. 'athena/records: force-push forbidden: in force', so Sri can see which host rule to set.
criteria_check.evidence: Test the_report_names_each_rule_and_its_state passed. It asserts the rendered lines for all three rules.

criteria_check.criterion: Doc comments cite D111 and docs/design/records-history.md §3 and describe this as part 3 of job 1; the module is registered in athena-core lib.rs.
criteria_check.evidence: Grep of host_rules.rs finds 5 matches for D111, §3 and 'part 3 of job 1'. The crate compiles with `pub mod host_rules;` in lib.rs.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test`: all clean and passing for the workspace.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo fmt --all --check` printed nothing. `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` finished clean. `cargo test --locked` returned no error. Its output was too large to read in full, and the preview showed no failure.

open_issues: I have not seen a real GitHub reply. The fixtures follow the documented shape.
Rules inherited from an organisation ruleset also appear in the rules/branches view. That is intended.
learnings: Tool output over the size limit is saved outside the working directory, and the Grep hook refuses to read it.
